docs.text: Course project Timeline Topic selection: Oct. 7, 2026 Final submission: Dec. 4, 2026 (further extended and firm deadline) Course projects should be done individually. Two options: Technical review Programming project Deliverable (Programming project) Proposal (5%): one-pager (one line or a short paragraph) Specify 1) the chosen topic, 2) programming language, and 3) tools or libraries you will use. Final report, code & demo (95%) Deliverable (Technical review) Proposal (5%): one-pager (one line or a short paragraph) Specify 1) the chosen topic and 2) the list of papers to read. Example topics: [ link ] Final report & presentation (95%): No less than 10 pages (format: 12-point font size on single-spaced 8.5" x 11" pages). Example technical review: [ pdf ] See suggested format ( not mandatory ) below. Format and grading criteria (Technical review) The report should cover 1) how it is an open research problem A technical review is intended to systematize the knowledge on a focused topic. The following is the suggested structure: Section 1 Paper Summaries Subsection 1.1: Summary of Paper P1 Problem studied in P1 Approach in P1 Evaluation result in P1 Technical novelty in P1 : How is the problem an open problem that prior research does not cover, or What technical challenges are presented in solving the problem? and How does the paper overcome the challenges? or How does the approach in the paper achieves a better or worse result compared to prior papers? In what metric and what quantity? Strength and limitation of P1 Subsection 1.2: Summary of Paper P2 ... Subsection 1.n: Summary of Paper Pn Section 2 Comparison Framework Defining m applicable properties F1 , F2 , F3 , ... The table for comparison (example below) Open problems and your prediction of future work. F1 F2 ... Fm P1 ✓ ✗ ... ✓ P2 ✗ ✓ ... ✓ Pn ✓ ✗ ... ✓
